text: The imaging and cystoscopy are normal, which effectively rules out structural abnormalities like stones, tumors, or severe infections. To distinguish between overactive bladder syndrome and interstitial cystitis, have you noticed any improvement or worsening of your symptoms when you reduce your fluid intake or consume acidic foods? REQUEST TEST: Post-Void Residual Volume.

speaker: Doctor
text: The post-void residual volume of 25 mL is low and normal, indicating good bladder emptying and ruling out significant obstruction or retention. Since we have effectively excluded infection, stones, tumors, and retention, have you experienced a sudden, compelling need to urinate that is difficult to defer, and do you wake up frequently at night to void?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome. The clinical picture of chronic pelvic pain relieved by voiding, frequency, and dyspareunia in a female with sterile urine and normal imaging is classic for this condition.
